UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT
FOR THE EASTERN DISTRICT OF VIRGINIA
ALEXANDRIA DIVISION
MARVELLE J. BALLENTINE,
Plaintiff,
Vv. Case No. 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD
The Honorable Judge

Ivan D. Davis

KATIE HALL, individually;
NATIONAL CENTER FOR MISSING & EXPLOITED CHILDREN;
META PLATFORMS, INC.;
and JOHN/JANE DOES 1-6,

Defendants.

PLAINTIFE’S REPLY IN SUPPORT OF MOTION UNDER FEDERAL
RULE OF CIVIL PROCEDURE 26(d)(1) FOR LEAVE TO SERVE
FOUR LIMITED INTERROGATORIES ON META PLATFORMS, INC.
BEFORE THE RULE 26(f) CONFERENCE

Plaintiff Marvelle J. Ballentine respectfully submits this Reply in support of his Motion
Under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 26(d)(1) for Leave to Serve Four Limited Interrogatories on
Meta Platforms, Inc. Before the Rule 26(f) Conference (ECF No. 54), and in reply to Defendant
Meta Platforms, Inc.’s Response in Opposition (ECF No. 73).

I. INTRODUCTION

Meta’s Opposition runs seven pages. ECF No. 73. It does not dispute that Meta’s
Memorandum described the April 22, 2026 letters as “the exact discovery” Plaintiff had sought
from Meta. ECF No. 22 at 9. It identifies no specific burden in answering four closed questions

about Meta’s own records. It asserts no privilege. It does not address the three-answer format, the

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD Document 81 Filed 09/21/26 Page 2 of 9 PagelD# 800

bounded period, or the Motion’s exclusion of all other discovery. ECF No. 54 at 2. Neither the
Opposition nor Meta’s dismissal briefing states whether Meta submitted a CyberTipline report
within the account and date parameters specified in Interrogatory No. 1. ECF Nos. 22, 39, 73. The
four interrogatories ask whether such a submission occurred and, if so, whether it contained or
otherwise identified the specified terms. ECF No. 54 at 1-2.

II. META HAS NOT ESTABLISHED THAT ITS PRELIMINARY-
INJUNCTION FRAMEWORK CONTROLS THIS REQUEST

Meta asks the Court to apply a modified preliminary-injunction test to this request. ECF
No. 73 at 2-3. Its principal authority, Arthur J. Gallagher & Co. v. Markfeld, addressed expedited
discovery in a preliminary-injunction proceeding. No. 3:25-cv-00885-RCY, ECF No. 70 at 1, 17—
18 (E.D. Va. July 29, 2026). Shenzhenshibairihongmaoyiyouxiangongsi v. Novoluto GmbH
likewise applied that framework to discovery sought for a pending preliminary injunction. No.
3:25-cv-00844-RCY, ECF No. 44 at 3-6 (E.D. Va. Mar. 9, 2026). Neither decision addressed the
four-question request presented here. Plaintiff identified that difference in ECF No. 55 at 4. The
Court retains authority under Rule 26(d)(1) to authorize discovery before the Rule 26(f) conference
and to confine that discovery to relevant, proportional inquiries under Rule 26(b)(1).

Plaintiff’s merits showing rests on the circumstances pleaded in the First Amended
Complaint, not on the proposition that the requested answers would establish a conspiracy. The
FAC alleges common receipt of case-specific materials, imminent examinations concerning
CyberTipline reporting, motions directed at that discovery, and two case-specific letters issued the
following day without compulsory process and without identifying the reporting provider or
account connection. FAC 4 126—135. Plaintiff relies on that combined sequence to support the
pleaded inference of agreement. ECF No. 30 at 12-14. Meta disputes that inference, in part by

characterizing its conduct and NCMEC’s conduct as contradictory because Meta sought to prevent

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD Document 81 Filed 09/21/26 Page 3 of 9 PagelD# 801

discovery that NCMEC supposedly supplied. ECF No. 22 at 9-10. The distinction between an
assertion about the discovery’s subject and the source-specific information sought is therefore
relevant to an argument Meta advances.

The reason for seeking the answers now is correspondingly specific. Meta invokes that
characterization in support of dismissal with prejudice, while the letters do not identify Meta as the
submitting provider or connect either report to Plaintiffs Facebook account. ECF No. 22 at 7, 9-
11, 14. Plaintiff’s existing declaration supplies a concrete basis for examining the listed identifiers:
Plaintiff states that he did not use his legal name to identify or operate a Meta account and included
it in the April 9 materials because it is his litigation name. ECF No. 31 4 3, 6—7. That declaration
does not establish what any report contained. It explains why the requested inquiry concerns
identified facts rather than an unrestricted search for a claim. ECF No. 55 at 3-4.

Novoluto supports considering informational imbalance and tailoring discovery to an
identified adjudicative need, but its irreparable-harm finding also rested on threatened marketplace
injuries and shifting seller identities. Novoluto, No. 3:25-cv-00844-RCY, ECF No. 44 at 5-6.
Plaintiff does not contend that a pending dismissal motion alone establishes irreparable harm or an
automatic entitlement to discovery. The requested exercise of discretion rests on the particular
factual issue, Plaintiff’s existing showing, the parties’ relative access to the information, and the
confined scope of four interrogatories. ECF No. 55 at 3—7.

Til. META’S CHARACTERIZATION OF THE LETTERS IS NOT AN
ESTABLISHED FACT
Meta’s Rule 12 papers tell the Court that NCMEC “provided him with exactly what he

asked for,” ECF No. 22 at 11, that the letters were “the exact discovery” Meta’s April 21 motion
practice sought to prevent, id. at 9, and that NCMEC was “responding to proposed subpoenas from

Plaintiff requesting the provided information,” ECF No. 39 at 5-6. Meta may argue from the

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD Document 81 Filed 09/21/26 Page 4 of 9 PagelD# 802

wording of the First Amended Complaint and the letters. Meta may not convert its characterization
of those documents into an established fact about reports the documents neither identify nor
produce. A court may consider a document without accepting its assertions, or a party’s assertions
about it, as true. Goines v. Valley Cmty. Servs. Bd., 822 F.3d 159, 166-69 (4th Cir. 2016). Plaintiff
has contested the asserted equivalence. ECF No. 30 at 6. The letters identify no reporting provider,
no account, and no enforcement event. ECF No. 22 at 7 (quoting FAC 4 92). The letters and the
cited paragraphs do not establish that Meta submitted a report concerning the account at issue.
Whether such a submission occurred is a question for inquiry into Meta’s reporting records, not a
fact established by its characterization of the letters. The four interrogatories address that inquiry.

The answers would be material without being conclusive. A “Yes” to Interrogatory No. 1
would establish that Meta submitted a report within the stated parameters. It would not, by itself,
establish that the submission was either report referenced in the April 22 letters. Interrogatories
Nos. 2 through 4 would identify whether a qualifying Meta submission contained or otherwise
identified the specified terms. ECF No. 54 at 1-2. No answer would adjudicate conspiracy,
intimidation, defamation, or liability. ECF No. 55 at 7. Plaintiff maintains that the FAC
independently pleads an agreement through the circumstances stated in FAC {J 124-138. The
requested discovery addresses the reporting facts relevant to Meta’s characterization of that alleged
conduct.

IV. THE SAME SUBJECT IS NOT THE SAME ANSWER

Meta reads two paragraphs of the First Amended Complaint as pleading the equivalence.
ECF No. 73 at 5. They do not. Paragraph 127 alleges that “the April 21, 2026 motions were directed
at the same discovery the April 9, 2026 materials described.” That is an allegation about what the

motions targeted. Paragraph 133 alleges that the letters “supplied, outside the discovery process, an

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD Document 81 Filed 09/21/26 Page 5 of 9 PagelD# 803

unsworn and source-free assertion concerning the precise subject scheduled for sworn
examination.” The Opposition quotes that paragraph as alleging that the letters “supplied. . . the
precise subject scheduled for sworn examination.” ECF No. 73 at 5. The ellipsis removes the words
“outside the discovery process, an unsworn and source-free assertion concerning.” Paragraph 133
alleges an unsworn assertion about the subject of the contemplated examination. Paragraph 135
alleges that the assertion “purported to answer” the report-existence question. Neither paragraph
concedes that the letters identified Meta as the submitting provider or connected either report to
Plaintiff’s Facebook account. Meta’s shortened quotation does not supply those missing
propositions.

Meta proposes that “[t]hat issue can be resolved based on the parties’ briefing.” ECF No. 73
at 5. The Court can determine from the FAC whether the cited paragraphs admit that Meta
submitted an account-related report. They do not. Whether Meta actually made such a submission
is a separate factual question that those paragraphs and the April 22 letters leave unanswered. The
four interrogatories address that question; they are not needed to establish what the FAC says.

V. THE CITED DECISIONS CONFIRM DISCRETION; THEY DO NOT
DECIDE THIS REQUEST

Rivers denied the early discovery requested there and stayed all discovery on the
defendants’ motion. ECF No. 73 at 4. Colonial River, as Meta quotes it, stayed discovery on a stay
motion after the court found the movants had made a colorable showing. Id. Those decisions
confirm the Court’s discretion to defer discovery. They do not establish that a pending dismissal
motion categorically defeats a request under Rule 26(d)(1). The question remains whether the
grounds stated in ECF No. 55 justify these four interrogatories now: one defendant, one identified
account, one bounded period, three permitted responses, and no production of any report. ECF No.

34 at 1-2.

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD Document 81 Filed 09/21/26 Page 6 of 9 PagelD# 804

The Opposition calls the dismissal of Case No. 1:26-cv-01341 “procedural
gamesmanship.” ECF No. 73 at 5. Rule 41(a)(1)(A)(i) conferred that dismissal as of right. The stay
entered in that action governed discovery in that action. It did not decide the four interrogatories
now proposed. It did not address Meta’s subsequently filed characterization of the April 22 letters.
The First Amended Complaint here was filed as of right under Rule 15(a)(1). ECF No. 59 10.
Plaintiff then sought leave to supplement under Rule 15(d), ECF No. 26, and now seeks leave to
file an amended and supplemental pleading, ECF No. 59. The present request is evaluated on the
present record.

VI. CONCLUSION

The Opposition identifies no specific burden, asserts no privilege, and contests neither the
scope nor the format of the four interrogatories. The answers are relevant to a characterization Meta
placed in its own Rule 12 briefing. Meta seeks dismissal with prejudice while the source-side facts
remain in Meta’s records. The request is confined to four answers about those records. The Motion
should be granted.

Date: September 21, 2026 Respectfully submitted,

Marvelle J. Ballentine

Plaintiff, pro se

CITATION CERTIFICATION PURSUANT TO ECF NOS. 63 AND 65

Pursuant to the Orders entered September 9, 2026 (ECF No. 63) and September 10, 2026
(ECF No. 65), Plaintiff states as follows.

1. Identification of use. Plaintiff used generative artificial intelligence in the preparation
of the Reply, the Certificate of Service, the Certification Pursuant to Local Civil Rule 83.1(N), and
this Disclosure and Certification. The assistance consisted of research, drafting, and revision of
text; retrieval of docket entries and filed documents from the public RECAP archive; and
verification of record citations against the docket. Plaintiff reviewed, edited, and adopted each
document as his own submission.

2. Citation review. Plaintiff certifies that he has reviewed each citation to legal authority
and each citation to the record in the documents identified in paragraph 1 for accuracy. Plaintiff
performed that review using automated citation-verification tools to verify cited authorities against
published sources and by comparing each record citation to the document as docketed.

3. Method. ECF Nos. 63 and 65 do not specify the form or placement of this disclosure.
Plaintiff places the disclosure and certification following the signature block of the filing it covers.
Plaintiff provides this disclosure and certification while maintaining the objections presented in
ECF Nos. 66 and 68.
